key_insight: DecisionRAG uses pretrained language models to make retrieval decisions rather than relying on keyword matches or fixed embedding similarity. It evaluates candidate document branches together in a single forward pass without generating tokens.
problem_solved: Retrieval can bottleneck otherwise capable language models: if relevant information is not found, the generator cannot use it. Conventional retrievers may miss information that requires more nuanced relevance judgments.
method: Frame document retrieval as navigation through candidate branches.
Use decision models to jointly evaluate candidate branches in one forward pass.
Make retrieval decisions without token generation, bringing pretrained language model capabilities into retrieval.
impact: The approach could help practitioners move beyond lexical and fixed-embedding retrieval bottlenecks. The supplied abstract is incomplete, so measured accuracy, latency, and efficiency gains cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: Side-by-side pipelines: conventional retriever → generator versus DecisionRAG navigation → generator.
A branching document tree with a query-guided path highlighted.
A single-forward-pass diagram showing candidate branches evaluated together.
A bottleneck illustration showing relevant evidence missed by retrieval and therefore unavailable to the generator.
paper_title: Retriever-Free Retrieval: Navigating Documents with Decision Models
paper_authors: Chao Wan, Paul Jünger, Beixi Du, Bodong Liu, Navaneetha Krishnan
